Chapter 10: Spreading Change — Scaling Up and Influencing Others
So, once change has really taken root in one area, the next big question is—how do you spread it further? Maybe it’s across your team, throughout your whole organization, or even out into the wider community. Scaling up change isn’t just about repeating the same steps everywhere. What works in one place might need a bit of tweaking somewhere else.
Here’s where it gets interesting: The trick is to figure out what key principles made your first change work so well. Once you know that, you can look for ways to recreate those wins, but you’ve got to stay flexible—every situation is a little different.
Sometimes, it’s about training fresh champions, sharing real stories of success, or putting together simple guides that others can easily pick up and use. If you’re thinking about how to spread change in a gentle, effective way, try these ideas:
First, document and share those bright spots. Capture what worked and why, then make it easy for others to find and learn from it.
Next, empower local leaders. Give people the tools and freedom to make the change fit their own context. When folks have a sense of ownership, they’re much more likely to stick with it.
And third, create frameworks that are simple and easy to share—think checklists, templates, or even quick stories that explain what’s possible. That way, anyone can understand and try it out for themselves.
Let’s make this real. Imagine a hospital that managed to cut infections in one unit. They could put together a toolkit for other departments—step-by-step instructions, plus testimonials from staff who’ve seen it work. Or picture a family that found a better rhythm for their daily routines. Maybe they share what’s working with friends or neighbors, helping each household adapt the ideas in their own way.
At the heart of it, scaling change isn’t about forcing everyone to do things exactly the same way. It’s about nurturing a whole network of local successes—letting change grow organically, rooted in the places where it’s most needed. By focusing on the principles that matter, and not getting hung up on rigid rules, you create space for meaningful, lasting change to spread far and wide.
